# THEORYs with `tags` `linguistics`

**Linguistics** — the study of language itself — morphology, lexicalism, word segmentation, syntax and semantics as linguists pose them, not as models encode them.

| [THEORY-017](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-017.md) v7 | Hilbert-space parts are extra data, not intrinsic | Carroll (2021), [LIT-123](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-123.md): a quantum theory is fixed up to unitary equivalence by the Hamiltonian's spectrum, and subsystems come from a factorisation that the dynamics must select. Van Rijsbergen ([LIT-262](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-262.md)) computes only traces and inner products, and treats each observable's eigenbasis as a "point of view". DisCoCat's ε/η composition ([LIT-273](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-273.md)) is orthogonally covariant, while its Frobenius sequel ([LIT-272](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-272.md)) stipulates a basis and composes by elementwise product in it. [THEORY-004](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-004.md) is the same point for learned representations. This is a synthesis across the four, not a result any one of them states. It does not say that basis-dependent models are wrong; it says what they have assumed. | Active |
| [THEORY-155](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-155.md) v3 | Bayesian iterated learning converges to the prior | Griffiths & Kalish (2007), [LIT-769](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-769.md), read in [NOTE-599](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-599.md): a chain of learners who share a prior and each sample a hypothesis from their posterior is a Gibbs sampler, so the probability a learner holds a hypothesis converges to its prior probability, whatever the amount of data passed on; with MAP learners the outcome centres on the prior's mode but depends on data amount and noise, and can amplify weak biases. It is a theorem about an idealized chain. It does not say human chains reach the prior, and Kirby, Cornish & Smith's laboratory chains, [LIT-771](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-771.md), are consistent with it without testing it. Whether human chains do is [QUESTION-137](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-137.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-159](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-159.md) | A term's value is set by its coexisting terms | Saussure (1916), [LIT-774](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-774.md), read in [NOTE-594](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-594.md), Part Two ch. IV. Value, the horizontal relation among signs, is distinguished from signification, the link inside one sign; the concept side and the sound side of a term are each "purely differential". It does not say that the sign as a whole is nothing but a difference: the book calls the sign a positive fact and the relation between signs opposition. The support is argument by example. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-162](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-162.md) | Context change is part of meaning | Heim (1982), [LIT-838](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-838.md); Veltman (1996), [LIT-818](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-818.md); Krifka (2024), [LIT-835](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-835.md). Three readings find, each in its own domain, sentences that agree in truth conditions or in the proposition they carry but differ in their effect on a conversational state. The effects are anaphoric potential (Heim), tests rather than information (Veltman), and changing indices rather than eliminating them (Krifka). This is the dynamic view: meaning as context-change potential. It does not say that truth conditions are irrelevant, since each framework recovers them, or that the three formalisms agree with each other. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-163](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-163.md) v5 | Colour naming lies near the bottleneck bound | Zaslavsky, Kemp, Regier & Tishby (2018), [LIT-810](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-810.md), read in [NOTE-631](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-631.md): treating a colour lexicon as an encoder from Gaussian perceptual meanings to words, the World Color Survey languages and English lie near the IB curve of [LIT-338](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-338.md) at β ≈ 1.03, beat hue-rotated variants of themselves, and their soft, partly inconsistent naming is what IB optima look like. It does not show that languages are driven to the bound by any process, and the need distribution that makes the fit best is estimated from the naming data themselves. | Active |
| [THEORY-164](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-164.md) v3 | Groups of eight built more systematic languages | Raviv, Meyer & Lev-Ari (2019), [LIT-825](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-825.md), read in [NOTE-628](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-628.md): fully connected groups of eight built more systematic languages than groups of four, faster and more uniformly, with total interaction and network structure fixed; input variability, larger in bigger groups, predicted the gains. One laboratory study, two group sizes, and a mechanism supported by lagged association, not manipulation. It says nothing yet about natural communities, where size travels with network density and second-language learners. | Active |
| [THEORY-170](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-170.md) v2 | Languages differ in what they oblige, not allow | Jakobson (1959), [LIT-786](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-786.md), after Boas: every cognitive content can be expressed in any language, but each grammar obliges its speakers to answer certain questions (aspect, number, gender, tense, definiteness). Translating between grammars that ask different questions forces the translator to supply answers the source did not give and to leave unexpressed answers it did, and a chain of translations of an isolated sentence can lose its content, less so the richer the context. Argued from examples, not tested; it concerns cognitive content, not pragmatic force. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-172](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-172.md) v5 | Listeners infer speakers choose by informativeness | Frank & Goodman (2012), [LIT-821](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-821.md), read in [NOTE-634](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-634.md): a parameter-free Bayesian listener inverting a size-principle speaker, with a separately measured salience prior, matches mean listener bets over seven context types at r = .99 (.87 without the 0 and 100 predictions), while salience alone correlates at r = .19. Bergen, Goodman & Levy (2012), [LIT-809](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-809.md), read in [NOTE-613](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-613.md): with novel signals and no conventions, listeners read the signal as the object its alternative did not name, and lexical uncertainty derives Horn's mapping. Goodman & Frank (2016), [LIT-816](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-816.md), states the framework. Shown for artificial games with given alternatives, by fits of condition means with no rival fitted; a test against named rivals on trial-level data is [QUESTION-209](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-209.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-204](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-204.md) v4 | Data-limited loss exponent overlaps γ/(2β) | Cagnetta, Raventós, Ganguli and Wyart (2026), [LIT-888](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-888.md), building on [LIT-883](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-883.md)'s effective context window. Under assumed scaling forms for the conditional entropy and for each lag's learning curve, the exponent is min(δ, γ/(2β)) (re-derived 2026-10-20). Measured on TinyStories and WikiText-103, with transformers up to about 10^8 tokens and horizons of tens of tokens, the fitted exponent overlaps γ/(2β), best near the start of the envelope; γ is estimated from trained models' own n-gram losses. Whether the horizon is why is open (QUESTION-233). | Active |
| [THEORY-271](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-271.md) v3 | Parallelepipeds need equiprobable sentences | Torii, Maeda and Hidaka (2024), [LIT-977](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-977.md), Theorem 1 (§5.5), read in full in [NOTE-781](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-781.md). Necessity is sound and short. The case analysis over permutations, and sufficiency, are loosely written. Exact shapes, raw counts, one design, and independent aspects that make the concept lattice Boolean. It says nothing about the logarithm or PMI, about noisy or approximate shapes, or about attributes that imply one another. | Active |
| [THEORY-477](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-477.md) | No cross-linguistic definition of word yet | Haspelmath (2011), [LIT-063](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-063.md), read in full in [NOTE-073](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-073.md). Each of ten criteria (pauses, free occurrence, mobility, uninterruptibility, non-selectivity, non-coordinatability, anaphoric islandhood, nonextractability, morphophonological idiosyncrasy, biuniqueness) fails as necessary and sufficient against cross-linguistic counterexamples, and nine published batteries use no common set (Table 1). The target is orthographic practice by design. It does not say that words cannot be defined within one language, that sub-word units are privileged, or that morphology and syntax are shown to be one domain; whether units cluster on a boundness scale is open. | Active |
| [THEORY-518](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-518.md) | Holism's meaning instability is local and graded | Grindrod, Porter and Hansen (2024), [LIT-208](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-208.md), read in full in [NOTE-158](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-158.md). The conceptual reply to the instability objection is argued; the empirical half is four hand-picked words in two before-and-after demonstrations (a count model on Stein plus a Hemingway story; Word2vec on Wikipedia plus the SEP), top-10 lists, one run each, no metric. The abstract's proportionality of resistance to frequency is not measured, the criterion used (a preserved neighbour list) is not the one defined (relative distances), and static embeddings only are tested. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-542](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-542.md) | Inferring speaker intent improves word learning | Frank, Goodman & Tenenbaum (2009), [LIT-815](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-815.md), read in [NOTE-611](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-611.md). On about twenty minutes of video from two dyads, annotated by the authors, the intentional model's lexicon scores precision .67 and F .55 against .06–.15 and .10–.22 for five baselines. The behavioural fits are qualitative, the baselines also produce mutual exclusivity, and the Baldwin case supplies the intention rather than inferring it. The reading said no THEORY, because the findings are specific to a small corpus and the record held nothing they correct; this account is filed Proposed for that reason. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-588](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-588.md) | Separate lemma stage fails polysynthesis, idioms | Krauska and Lau (2023), [LIT-031](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-031.md), read in full in [NOTE-029](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-029.md). A Hypothesis and Theory article with no new data and no implementation. The 8-stage replacement model and its aphasia predictions are a verbal sketch, and this account does not rest on them. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-623](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-623.md) v2 | Language-data contextuality is not secured | Lo, Sadrzadeh & Mansfield (2024), [LIT-844](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-844.md), read in [NOTE-648](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-648.md), and Wang, Sadrzadeh, Abramsky & Cervantes (2021), [LIT-842](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-842.md), read in [NOTE-645](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-645.md). | [THEORY-643](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-643.md) | One component can build words and phrases | Bruening (2018), [LIT-071](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-071.md), read in full in [NOTE-065](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-065.md). Phrases feed English word formation productively, ellipsis and focus reach sub-word units, and claimed differences of principle (locality, adjuncts, headedness, idiosyncrasy) fail; extraction, coordination and the no-phrase constraint are restated over X0 vs XP and affix selection, with no mention of "word". The English evidence of §§2–3 is the strong part. Several sub-arguments are provisional by the author's own account, and Müller's reply in the same volume disputes extraction, coordination and the resultative argument. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-670](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-670.md) | Dispositions are restricted possibilities | Vetter (2014), [LIT-109](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-109.md), read in full from the penultimate draft in [NOTE-125](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-125.md). A proposal, which the paper says it does not show superior to the conditional conception (pp. 6, 26). Its strongest part is negative: for any ideal world, an Achilles'-heel block that breaks only there counts as fragile, so closeness grading fails. The positive proportion measure is not defined, and the finite, maximally varied set of cases it counts over is admitted to be non-unique. The evidence is '-able' semantics and a COCA count in which none of 226 relevant uses of "disposed to" ascribes a standing tendency to an inanimate object. Finks and masks are left unsolved, and dispositions of fundamental science are set aside. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-693](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-693.md) | Evaluation, positioning, alignment: one stance | Du Bois (2007), [LIT-779](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-779.md), read in full in [NOTE-590](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-590.md). The co-occurrence of the three aspects is shown in chosen examples, not tested for separability; the too/either result rests on a separate study (Du Bois 2004) whose figures are not given. It does not treat a speaker who animates someone else's stance, which it sets aside for Goffman. | Proposed |

| [THEORY-1004](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1004.md) | Agreement features shift from tokens to grammar | Bayazit, Mueller and Bosselut (2025, ACL 2026), [LIT-1555](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1555.md), read in [NOTE-1186](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1186.md). Crosscoders trained jointly on the middle layer of two or three checkpoints, with features scored by their relative indirect effect on agreement minimal pairs at each. | [THEORY-1131](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1131.md) | LLMs choose Indic pragmatic readings, lean literal | Singh et al. (2026), [LIT-1817](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1817.md), read in [NOTE-1345](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1345.md) from the Findings of EMNLP 2026 PDF. MCQ beat NLI in 20 of 20 model–language pairs (recomputed). 59.1% of wrong MCQ answers took the literal distractor, against 33.3% by chance, and 53.8% of Contradiction items were labelled Entailment. The gold answers are each language's one item author's reading, cells hold 5–16 items, and the MCQ and NLI sets are different items. So "recognizing and reasoning about pragmatic meaning are distinct competencies" is the authors' gloss, not a finding. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1144](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1144.md) | Politeness classifier transfers but trails natives | Srinivasan and Choi (2022), [LIT-1799](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1799.md), read in [NOTE-1339](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1339.md). The judges were screened for agreeing with this classifier, and the extreme items were chosen on a mean that includes the held-out judge, so the gap and the transfer are both measured on favourable ground. | Proposed |
